paper.title_en: Shadow bootstrapping: Nearly minimal-setting pure-state tomography with shallow Clifford measurements
paper.abstract_en: We present a pure-state tomography algorithm that uses a nearly minimal number of measurement settings while achieving optimal sample complexity with nonadaptive single-copy shallow Clifford measurements. For an arbitrary $n$-qubit pure state $|ψ\rangle \in \mathbb{C}^{d}$, where $d=2^n$, the algorithm uses $O(d/ε)$ copies and $\widetilde{O}(1)$ measurement settings to output a state vector $|\hatψ\rangle$ satisfying $1-|\langleψ|\hatψ\rangle|^2\leε$ with high probability. Each measurement is implemented by a Clifford circuit of depth $O(\log n)$. Reusing each measurement setting allows the data to be stored compactly as per-basis outcome histograms. Given these histograms, classical post-processing runs in $\widetilde{O}(d)$ time. Our key technique, \textit{shadow bootstrapping}, uses the current estimate to reduce the variance of subsequent residual estimation, enabling progressively more accurate reconstruction with only a constant number of new measurement settings per stage.
